logline: Monday. The counter: forty thousand a day. Wood can't draw forty thousand, so he draws one stick figure and writes × 40,000 beside it, and the strip is about the multiplication sign.

panels.composition: The garage. The CRT: a counter, 40,012. WOOD looking at it. BARNABY.

image.prompt: brush-pen line with muddy early-digital flats, a man looking at a CRT monitor showing a five-digit visitor counter in a dark garage, a small dog beside him

panels.composition: The pad. One stick figure. Beside it, in the display face: × 40,000.

image.prompt: brush-pen line with muddy early-digital flats, close-up of a drawing pad with a single crude stick figure and a large multiplication sign and number lettered beside it

panels.composition: Wood, to the dog, about the sign.

balloons.text: I can draw one. I can draw one very well. I can't draw the times.
The times is the part that's happening.

image.prompt: brush-pen line with muddy early-digital flats, a man speaking to a small dog while holding a pad with a single figure and a multiplication sign on it

panels.composition: The garage. The chorus at the back — thirty — and behind them, drawn as a texture to the panel's edge and past it: more. The one figure on the pad. The ×.

image.prompt: brush-pen line with muddy early-digital flats, a garage with a man and a dog in the foreground and thirty crude stick figures at the back dissolving into a dense texture of thousands more past the panel's edge, no words

art.palette: limited; Sundays in watercolor, good now
art.paper: bristol; the browser; from 2008 coastal newsprint a week behind
